# `fenrir-ts/2d` API reference

Generated from the TSDoc in the source by `scripts/api-reference.mjs`. Do not edit: run `pnpm api:reference`.

The `pixi2d` plugin, layers, the design-frame viewport, `PixiNode`, `Renderable2D` and the 2D builder methods.

Peer packages: `pixi.js`. Import from `fenrir-ts/2d` only, never from `dist/` or a source path.

## Contents

- Functions: [`createPixiRendererSystem`](#createpixirenderersystem), [`createPixiTextureLoader`](#createpixitextureloader), [`layoutViewport`](#layoutviewport), [`logicalToScreen`](#logicaltoscreen), [`pixi2d`](#pixi2d), [`screenToLogical`](#screentological)
- Classes: [`PixiRenderer`](#pixirenderer)
- Constants: [`PixiNode`](#pixinode), [`Renderable2D`](#renderable2d), [`Viewport`](#viewport), [`ViewportResized`](#viewportresized)
- Types: [`ContainerDesc`](#containerdesc), [`GraphicsDesc`](#graphicsdesc), [`Pixi2DOptions`](#pixi2doptions), [`Pixi2DPlugin`](#pixi2dplugin), [`PixiRendererOptions`](#pixirendereroptions), [`PixiRendererSystemOptions`](#pixirenderersystemoptions), [`PixiTextureLoaderConfig`](#pixitextureloaderconfig), [`Render2DFlags`](#render2dflags), [`SpriteDesc`](#spritedesc), [`TextDesc`](#textdesc), [`Texture2DHandle`](#texture2dhandle), [`Texture2DState`](#texture2dstate), [`ViewportDesign`](#viewportdesign), [`ViewportInsets`](#viewportinsets), [`ViewportPoint`](#viewportpoint)
- [Added to core types when imported](#added-to-core-types-when-imported)
- Re-exported from `fenrir-ts`: `Display2D`, `Transform2D`

## Functions

### createPixiRendererSystem

```ts
function createPixiRendererSystem(opts: PixiRendererSystemOptions): { renderer: PixiRenderer; init: (ctx: SystemCtx) => Promise<void>; postUpdate: (ctx: SystemCtx) => void; exit: (ctx: SystemCtx) => void; };
```

The renderer's systems without the plugin, for tests that drive `init`, `postUpdate` and `exit` by hand. Games use `pixi2d()`.

### createPixiTextureLoader

```ts
function createPixiTextureLoader(): AssetLoader<Texture>;
```

The default `texture2d` loader: Pixi's `Assets.load`. `pixi2d()` registers it.

### layoutViewport

```ts
function layoutViewport(design: ViewportDesign, screen: {
    readonly width: number;
    readonly height: number;
}, insets: ViewportInsets, resolution: number): Viewport;
```

Lays the design frame out on a screen. The design width fills the safe area's width, and the
logical height grows to fill its height; a safe area too short for `minHeight` scales the
frame down further, keeps the height at `minHeight` and centres the frame horizontally.
`pixi2d({ design })` uses it to set the `Viewport` resource. It is pure, so browser tests can
turn design units into click positions with the same rule: `logicalToScreen(layout, point)`.

```ts
const layout = layoutViewport({ width: 390, minHeight: 520 }, { width: 390, height: 844 }, { top: 47, right: 0, bottom: 34, left: 0 }, 3);
logicalToScreen(layout, { x: 195, y: 100 }); // CSS pixels from the canvas corner
```

### logicalToScreen

```ts
function logicalToScreen(viewport: Viewport, point: ViewportPoint): ViewportPoint;
```

Converts a point in logical units into CSS pixels from the canvas's top-left corner.

### pixi2d

```ts
function pixi2d(options?: Pixi2DOptions): Pixi2DPlugin;
```

The PixiJS 2D renderer as a game plugin. Registers `fenrir.pixi.init` (Init),
`fenrir.viewport.init` (Init, after it), `fenrir.viewport.preUpdate` (PreUpdate, applies resizes),
`fenrir.pixi.postUpdate` (PostUpdate: writes `Transform2D` and `Display2D` to `PixiNode` and
`Renderable2D` entities, then renders; `renderer.render()` does the same sync) and `fenrir.pixi.exit` (Exit, unmounts and destroys nodes). Keeps the `Viewport` resource and sends `ViewportResized`.

```ts
const pixi = pixi2d({ design: { width: 390, minHeight: 520 }, background: 0x101820 });
const game = await createGame({ canvas, plugins: [pixi] });
pixi.renderer.root; // draw here in design units, once the game runs
```

### screenToLogical

```ts
function screenToLogical(viewport: Viewport, point: ViewportPoint): ViewportPoint | null;
```

Converts a point on the screen (CSS pixels from the canvas's top-left corner) into logical
units. Returns null while the viewport has no area (scale 0).

## Classes

### PixiRenderer

```ts
class PixiRenderer {
    readonly root: PIXI.Container<PIXI.ContainerChild>;
    readonly backdrop: PIXI.Container<PIXI.ContainerChild>;
    constructor(options: PixiRendererOptions);
    layer(name: string): PIXI.Container;
    attachNode(entities: EntityList, entity: Entity, value: PixiNode): void;
    detachNode(entity: Entity, value: PixiNode): void;
    releaseNodes(entities: EntityList | undefined): void;
    unmountNodes(): void;
    get app(): PIXI.Application;
    init(): Promise<void>;
    get initialized(): boolean;
    resize(width: number, height: number, resolution?: number): void;
    applyViewport(viewport: Viewport): void;
    clientToLogical(clientX: number, clientY: number): ViewportPoint | null;
    logicalToClient(x: number, y: number): ViewportPoint | null;
    upsertRenderable(entities: EntityList, entity: Entity, renderable: Renderable2D): Promise<void>;
    removeRenderable(entity: Entity, renderId: number): void;
    syncTransforms(entities: EntityList): void;
    bindScene(entities: EntityList | undefined): void;
    render(): void;
    clearRenderables(): void;
    dispose(): void;
    getRenderedObject(entity: Entity, renderableId: number): PIXI.Container | undefined;
}
```

The 2D renderer behind `pixi2d()`, as `plugin.renderer`. Game code adds Pixi content to `root` (logical units) or `backdrop` (full-bleed CSS pixels), or reads a named layer with `layer(name)`.

Members:

- `root`: Game content, drawn in logical units. `pixi2d` scales and positions it to the design frame; without `design` it is unscaled at the top-left. Entities with `Renderable2D` mount here.
- `backdrop`: Full-bleed content behind `root`, in CSS pixels from the screen's top-left corner, unscaled. Cover `Viewport.screen` to fill the whole screen, outside the frame and the safe area too.
- `layer`: The container of a layer from `pixi2d({ layers })`: a child of `root`, in logical units, its children sorted by `zIndex`. `"fenrir.backdrop"` returns `backdrop`. Throws for an unknown name, listing the declared ones.
- `attachNode`: Mounts an entity's `PixiNode`, replacing the node it had. Internal: the renderer system calls it.
- `detachNode`: Unmounts `value.node` after an entity's `PixiNode` was removed. Internal.
- `releaseNodes`: Unmounts every node at stop. Destroys the ones not kept and removes their `PixiNode` components, so a later run never mounts a destroyed node. Internal.
- `unmountNodes`: Unmounts every node without destroying any, when the active scene changes. Internal.
- `applyViewport`: Places `root` for `viewport`: at its offset, at its scale. Called by `pixi2d` when the layout changes. Internal.
- `clientToLogical`: Converts CSS client coordinates (a DOM event's `clientX`, `clientY`) into logical units: design units with `pixi2d({ design })`. Returns null while the canvas or frame has no area.
- `logicalToClient`: Converts logical units into CSS client coordinates. The inverse of `clientToLogical`.
- `syncTransforms`: Writes transforms to every node and renderable view and mounts each under its parent. Runs once a frame, before rendering. Internal.
- `bindScene`: Sets the entities `render()` syncs. Internal: the renderer system binds the active scene.
- `render`: Syncs every node and view with its entity's `Transform2D` and `Display2D`, then renders. `fenrir.pixi.postUpdate` calls it each frame; game code may call it to draw outside a frame, for example from a startup system, and sees the same synced scene.

## Constants

### PixiNode

```ts
type PixiNode = {
    readonly node: Container;
    readonly layer?: string;
    readonly keep?: boolean;
};
const PixiNode: ComponentType<PixiNode>;
```

A Pixi display object the app built, owned by an entity. The 2D renderer mounts `node` in
`layer` (a name from `pixi2d({ layers })`), or under the node of the entity's parent when the
parent has one, or in `renderer.root`. `layer: "fenrir.backdrop"` mounts it in
`renderer.backdrop` instead, where `Transform2D` is in CSS pixels from the screen's corner.
Every render writes the entity's `Transform2D` and `Display2D` to it first; without them the
app positions and shows the node itself. A child entity's node sorts by `zIndex` under its
parent's node: Pixi turns `sortableChildren` on when a child has a non-zero `zIndex`.

When the component or the entity is removed, or the run stops, the renderer removes `node`
from its parent and destroys it with its children (not their textures). With `keep: true` it
only removes it from its parent, and at stop the component stays so the next run mounts it
again. A destroyed node's component is removed at stop.

### Renderable2D

```ts
type Renderable2D = {
    readonly id: number;
    sprite?: SpriteDesc;
    graphics?: GraphicsDesc;
    text?: TextDesc;
    container?: ContainerDesc;
    flags?: Render2DFlags;
};
const Renderable2D: ComponentType<Renderable2D>;
```

Core 2D rendering component for PixiJS-based entities

### Viewport

```ts
interface Viewport {
    readonly width: number;
    readonly height: number;
    readonly scale: number;
    readonly offset: ViewportPoint;
    readonly insets: ViewportInsets;
    readonly screen: {
        readonly width: number;
        readonly height: number;
    };
    readonly resolution: number;
}
const Viewport: ResourceType<Viewport>;
```

Where the game's logical frame sits on the screen. Plain data: a new object each time the
layout changes, so a held reference is a snapshot.

"Screen" is the canvas, in CSS pixels from its top-left corner.

Members:

- `width`: Logical width: the design width, or the screen width without `design`.
- `height`: Logical height: at least the design's `minHeight`, or the screen height without `design`.
- `scale`: CSS pixels per logical unit. 0 while the safe area is empty.
- `offset`: Top-left corner of the logical frame on the screen, in CSS pixels.
- `insets`: Safe-area insets in use, in CSS pixels. All 0 with `safeArea: false` or without `design`.
- `screen`: The whole screen (the canvas), in CSS pixels. Full-bleed content covers this.
- `resolution`: Backing-store pixels per CSS pixel: `devicePixelRatio`, capped by `maxResolution`.

### ViewportResized

```ts
const ViewportResized: EventType<Viewport>;
```

Sent with the new `Viewport` once at startup and whenever the layout changes after that.

## Types

### ContainerDesc

```ts
type ContainerDesc = {
    readonly kind: "container";
    readonly children?: readonly number[];
};
```

Container descriptor for grouping display objects

### GraphicsDesc

```ts
type GraphicsDesc = {
    readonly kind: "graphics";
    readonly shape: "rect" | "circle" | "polygon";
    readonly fillColor?: number;
    readonly strokeColor?: number;
    readonly strokeWidth?: number;
    readonly data?: unknown;
};
```

Graphics descriptor for procedural drawing

### Pixi2DOptions

```ts
interface Pixi2DOptions {
    readonly design?: ViewportDesign;
    readonly safeArea?: boolean;
    readonly maxResolution?: number;
    readonly background?: number;
    readonly application?: PIXI.Application;
    readonly width?: number;
    readonly height?: number;
    readonly layers?: readonly string[];
    readonly applicationOptions?: PixiRendererOptions["applicationOptions"];
}
```

What `pixi2d()` takes: the design frame, layers, background and Pixi application options. Every field is optional.

Members:

- `design`: The size the game is designed for, in logical units. With it the plugin owns the canvas size: the canvas fills the window, the design width fills the safe area's width, and the logical height grows from `minHeight` to fill its height. A safe area too short for `minHeight` scales the frame down and centres it horizontally. Game content in `renderer.root` is drawn in these units. Without it, logical units are CSS pixels and the canvas keeps the size it was created with.
- `safeArea`: With `design`, lay the frame out inside `env(safe-area-inset-*)`. Defaults to true.
- `maxResolution`: Caps backing-store pixels per CSS pixel: `min(devicePixelRatio, maxResolution)`. Defaults to 2.
- `background`: Clear colour, as 0xRRGGBB. A Pixi application the plugin creates defaults to 0x101010. An adopted `application` keeps its own unless this is given, which sets it when Init runs.
- `application`: A Pixi application the app already owns, initialized on the game's canvas with its ticker stopped. The game renders it but does not destroy it at exit.
- `width`: Size of a Pixi application the plugin creates, without `design`. Defaults to the window size.
- `layers`: Named layers under `renderer.root`, back to front. An entity's `PixiNode` picks one by name; `renderer.layer(name)` returns its container. Content added straight to `root` draws above every layer, and `renderer.backdrop` stays behind them all; a `PixiNode` mounts there with the layer name `"fenrir.backdrop"`. Names starting with `fenrir.` are reserved and throw.
- `applicationOptions`: Other initialization options for a Pixi application the plugin creates.

### Pixi2DPlugin

```ts
interface Pixi2DPlugin extends Plugin {
    readonly renderer: PixiRenderer;
}
```

What `pixi2d()` returns: a plugin for `createGame`, with the renderer it installs.

Members:

- `renderer`: The renderer, for game code that draws with Pixi directly: add content to `renderer.root` (logical units, scaled to the design frame) or `renderer.backdrop` (full-bleed, CSS pixels). Available once `createGame` has installed the plugin; its Pixi application is initialized when the game's Init stage runs.

### PixiRendererOptions

```ts
interface PixiRendererOptions {
    readonly canvas?: HTMLCanvasElement;
    readonly logger: ILogger;
    readonly width?: number;
    readonly height?: number;
    readonly clearColor?: number;
    readonly assets: IAssetStore;
    readonly application?: PIXI.Application;
    readonly applicationOptions?: Partial<Omit<PIXI.ApplicationOptions, "canvas" | "autoStart" | "sharedTicker">>;
    readonly layers?: readonly string[];
}
```

Options of the 2D renderer, passed through `pixi2d()`.

Members:

- `clearColor`: Clear colour as 0xRRGGBB. An engine-owned application defaults to 0x101010; an adopted one is set to it at init when given.
- `application`: An initialized application owned by the caller, with its automatic ticker stopped.
- `applicationOptions`: Initialization options for an engine-owned application.
- `layers`: Named layers under `root`, back to front. Names starting with `fenrir.` are reserved.

### PixiRendererSystemOptions

```ts
interface PixiRendererSystemOptions extends PixiRendererOptions {
}
```

What `createPixiRendererSystem` takes.

```ts
type PixiTextureLoaderConfig = LoaderConfig<PixiTexture>;
```

```ts
type SpriteDesc = {
```

### TextDesc

```ts
type TextDesc = {
    readonly kind: "text";
    readonly content: string;
    readonly style?: {
        readonly fontFamily?: string;
        readonly fontSize?: number;
        readonly fill?: number;
        readonly align?: "left" | "center" | "right";
    };
};
```

Text descriptor for text rendering

### Texture2DHandle

```ts
interface Texture2DHandle {
    readonly state: Texture2DState;
    readonly ready: Promise<PixiTexture>;
    subscribe(listener: (state: Texture2DState) => void): () => void;
}
```

What `assets.requestTexture2D(key)` returns: the texture once loaded, and where its load stands.

Members:

- `subscribe`: Observes the transition out of loading. Read state for the current value.

### Texture2DState

```ts
type Texture2DState = {
    readonly status: "loading";
} | {
    readonly status: "ready";
    readonly texture: PixiTexture;
} | {
    readonly status: "failed";
    readonly error: unknown;
};
```

Where a `Texture2DHandle`'s load stands.

### ViewportDesign

```ts
interface ViewportDesign {
    readonly width: number;
    readonly minHeight: number;
}
```

The size a 2D game is designed for, in logical units. See `pixi2d({ design })`.

Members:

- `width`: Logical width. Always fits the safe area exactly.
- `minHeight`: Least logical height. The height grows past it to fill taller screens.

### ViewportInsets

```ts
interface ViewportInsets {
    readonly top: number;
    readonly right: number;
    readonly bottom: number;
    readonly left: number;
}
```

Distances in CSS pixels from each edge of the screen.

### ViewportPoint

```ts
interface ViewportPoint {
    readonly x: number;
    readonly y: number;
}
```

A point in CSS pixels or in logical units.

## Added to core types when imported

Importing `fenrir-ts/2d` adds these members to core types for the whole program.

### AssetKinds

```ts
interface AssetKinds {
    texture2d: PixiTexture;
}
```

### AssetStoreConfig

```ts
interface AssetStoreConfig {
    texture2DLoaders?: {
        [name: string]: PixiTextureLoaderConfig;
    };
}
```

### IAssetStore

```ts
interface IAssetStore {
    loadTexture2D(key: AssetKey, url: string): Promise<void>;
    getTexture2D(key: AssetKey): Promise<PixiTexture>;
    registerTexture2DLoader(name: string, config: PixiTextureLoaderConfig): void;
    getSupportedTexture2DExtensions(): string[];
}
```

### AssetStore

```ts
interface AssetStore {
    loadTexture2D(key: AssetKey, url: string): Promise<void>;
    requestTexture2D(key: AssetKey, url: string): Texture2DHandle;
    getTexture2D(key: AssetKey): Promise<PixiTexture>;
    registerTexture2DLoader(name: string, config: PixiTextureLoaderConfig): void;
    getSupportedTexture2DExtensions(): string[];
}
```

- `requestTexture2D`: Reuses an active or ready request for the same key and URL. Request again to retry a failure.

### EntityBuilder

```ts
interface EntityBuilder {
    pixiNode(node: Container, options?: {
        layer?: string;
        keep?: boolean;
    }): this;
    renderSprite(texture: string, options?: {
        anchor?: readonly [
            number,
            number
        ];
        tint?: number;
        flags?: Render2DFlags;
    }): this;
    renderCircle(radius: number, options?: {
        fillColor?: number;
        strokeColor?: number;
        strokeWidth?: number;
        flags?: Render2DFlags;
    }): this;
    renderRect(width: number, height: number, options?: {
        fillColor?: number;
        strokeColor?: number;
        strokeWidth?: number;
        flags?: Render2DFlags;
    }): this;
    renderText(content: string, options?: {
        style?: {
            readonly fontFamily?: string;
            readonly fontSize?: number;
            readonly fill?: number;
            readonly align?: "left" | "center" | "right";
        };
        flags?: Render2DFlags;
    }): this;
}
```

- `pixiNode`: Gives the entity a Pixi display object the app built (`PixiNode`). Mounted in `layer`, or
 under the parent entity's node; destroyed with the entity unless `keep` is true.
- `renderSprite`: Add a 2D sprite renderable
- `renderCircle`: Add a 2D circle graphic
- `renderRect`: Add a 2D rectangle graphic
- `renderText`: Add 2D text renderable

<!-- skills/fenrir/api/ui.md -->

# `fenrir-ts/ui` API reference

Generated from the TSDoc in the source by `scripts/api-reference.mjs`. Do not edit: run `pnpm api:reference`.

Controls and modal scopes on Pixi nodes the game drew, driven by the engine's input.

Peer packages: `pixi.js`. Import from `fenrir-ts/ui` only, never from `dist/` or a source path.

## Contents

- Functions: [`activateControl`](#activatecontrol), [`control`](#control), [`listControls`](#listcontrols), [`modalScope`](#modalscope), [`moveFocus`](#movefocus), [`paginate`](#paginate), [`syncUi`](#syncui), [`ui`](#ui)
- Constants: [`ControlActivated`](#controlactivated), [`UiFocus`](#uifocus)
- Types: [`Activation`](#activation), [`ControlBounds`](#controlbounds), [`ControlInfo`](#controlinfo), [`ControlOptions`](#controloptions), [`FocusRingDrawer`](#focusringdrawer), [`HitArea`](#hitarea), [`ModalScopeOptions`](#modalscopeoptions), [`UiCtx`](#uictx), [`UiKeys`](#uikeys), [`UiOptions`](#uioptions)
- [Added to core types when imported](#added-to-core-types-when-imported)

## Functions

### activateControl

```ts
function activateControl(game: UiCtx, id: string): boolean;
```

Activates the live, unblocked control `id` as a tap would, with `via: "call"`, while the game
runs. Returns false, activating nothing, when no such control is live or it is disabled.

### control

```ts
function control<T extends Container>(node: T, options: ControlOptions): T;
```

Makes `node`, which the game drew, a control: tappable and focusable while it is in the scene,
visible and renderable, and gone once it is destroyed. Calling it again replaces the options.
Returns `node`.

### listControls

```ts
function listControls(game: UiCtx): ControlInfo[];
```

The live controls now, unblocked ones first in focus order, then those a modal scope blocks.

### modalScope

```ts
function modalScope<T extends Container>(node: T, options: ModalScopeOptions): T;
```

Makes `node` a modal scope: while it is live, only controls inside it take taps and focus,
every tap is kept from the game, and the `close` keys call `onClose`. Scopes nest: the one
shown last is on top. It ends when the node is hidden, removed or destroyed. Focus does not
carry from one scope to another, even to a control with the same id. Returns `node`.

### moveFocus

```ts
function moveFocus(game: UiCtx, delta: number, wrap?: boolean): string | null;
```

Moves focus `delta` places in focus order among the live, unblocked controls, and shows the
ring, as an arrow key does. From no focus, `1` goes to the first control and `-1` to the
last. Stops at the ends, or wraps round with `wrap`. Takes `game` or a system's `ctx`; returns
the focused id, `null` when no control is live.

### paginate

```ts
function paginate<T>(rows: readonly T[], capacity: number, page: number): {
    rows: T[];
    page: number;
    pages: number;
};
```

The page of `rows` that holds `capacity` rows per page. `page` is clamped into range, so a
list that shrank shows its last page; an empty list has one empty page.

### syncUi

```ts
function syncUi(game: UiCtx): void;
```

Brings the ring, the cursor and the canvas's `aria-label` and `aria-description` up to date
now. The kit does this after `Update` each frame (`fenrir.ui.postUpdate`) and before the game's
`PostInit` systems (`fenrir.ui.postInit`); call it after drawing controls in a later system and
before rendering, such as in a `PostInit` system that renders the first frame. While the game runs.

### ui

```ts
function ui(options?: UiOptions): Plugin;
```

The controls kit as a plugin: list it after `pixi2d` and pass that plugin, `ui({ pixi })`.
Registers `fenrir.ui.init` (Init: the ring and the canvas's saved attributes),
`fenrir.ui.preUpdate` (PreUpdate, before the game's own: keys, pointer presses and the game's
`actions` in the order they arrived), and `fenrir.ui.postInit` and `fenrir.ui.postUpdate`
(before the game's PostInit systems, and after Update before the renderer: the ring, cursor and
accessibility output, so they match the frame that is drawn). A game system that must see a
press before the kit runs passes `{ before: "fenrir.ui.preUpdate" }`.

## Constants

### ControlActivated

```ts
const ControlActivated: EventType<{ readonly id: string; readonly via: Activation; }>;
```

Sent each time a control activates, after its `onActivate`.

### UiFocus

```ts
interface UiFocus {
    id: string | null;
    visible: boolean;
}
const UiFocus: ResourceType<UiFocus>;
```

The focused control. Set `id` to move focus. It is cleared whenever the kit reads the display
tree and that control is not live or a modal scope blocks it: at the start and end of its pass,
after each activation, `onClose` and `onAction`, and in `syncUi`.

Members:

- `visible`: Show the ring: true after a key moves focus, false after a tap. The ring also needs the canvas focused.

## Types

### Activation

```ts
type Activation = "pointer" | "key" | "call";
```

How a control was activated: a pointer tap, a key on the focused control, or `activateControl`.

### ControlBounds

```ts
interface ControlBounds {
    readonly x: number;
    readonly y: number;
    readonly width: number;
    readonly height: number;
}
```

An axis-aligned box in logical units: design units with `pixi2d({ design })`.

### ControlInfo

```ts
interface ControlInfo {
    readonly id: string;
    readonly label: string;
    readonly disabled: boolean;
    readonly focused: boolean;
    readonly blocked: boolean;
    readonly bounds: ControlBounds;
}
```

One live control, as `listControls(game)` and `inspect(game)` report it.

Members:

- `focused`: `UiFocus.id` is this control.
- `blocked`: Outside the top modal scope: takes no taps, focus or `activateControl`.
- `bounds`: The hit area's box in logical units, computed from the nodes' transforms, so correct in a test game that never renders: turn it into a click with `logicalToScreen`.

### ControlOptions

```ts
interface ControlOptions {
    readonly id: string;
    readonly label: string;
    readonly onActivate?: (ctx: SystemCtx, via: Activation) => void;
    readonly disabled?: boolean;
    readonly hitArea?: HitArea;
    readonly order?: number;
    readonly activateOn?: "press" | "release";
    readonly passThrough?: boolean;
}
```

What `control(node, options)` takes. `id` is required and must be unique among live controls.

Members:

- `id`: Names the control: focus, `ControlActivated`, `activateControl` and tests use it. Unique among live controls.
- `label`: What the control does, for people: the canvas's `aria-description` reads `Focused: <label>`.
- `onActivate`: Runs when the control activates, inside `fenrir.ui.preUpdate` (or `activateControl`), before `ControlActivated` is sent.
- `disabled`: Still takes focus and taps (so the press does not fall through to the game) but never activates.
- `hitArea`: Overrides the hit area, in the node's own units. Defaults to the node's local bounds.
- `order`: Focus order: lower first, ties in display order. Defaults to 0.
- `activateOn`: When a pointer activates the control. `"release"` (the default): a press and a release over it, in the frame that reports the release. `"press"`: in the frame of the press, for a button that times a tap; sliding off or cancelling then changes nothing. Keys always act on the press.
- `passThrough`: Lets a pointer press on the control through to the game: the kit does not consume it, so gameplay systems still see `pressed`, even inside a modal scope. The control still takes focus and taps and activates as `activateOn` says. The `activate` keys on the focused control are left unconsumed too, so gameplay sees Enter or Space as its own press. Either way the press is the kit's: it does not reach `onAction`.

### FocusRingDrawer

```ts
type FocusRingDrawer = (ring: Graphics, bounds: ControlBounds, control: ControlInfo) => void;
```

Draws the focus ring into `ring`, which the kit has cleared, around `bounds` (logical units).

### HitArea

```ts
type HitArea = {
    readonly x: number;
    readonly y: number;
    readonly width: number;
    readonly height: number;
} | {
    readonly x: number;
    readonly y: number;
    readonly radius: number;
};
```

A hit area in the node's own units: a rectangle, or a circle for round buttons. Pixi's `Rectangle` and `Circle` fit.

### ModalScopeOptions

```ts
interface ModalScopeOptions {
    readonly label: string;
    readonly onClose?: (ctx: SystemCtx) => void;
    readonly focus?: string;
}
```

What `modalScope(node, options)` takes. While a scope is live, only controls inside it take input.

Members:

- `label`: The canvas's `aria-label` while this scope is on top, such as `"Shop"`.
- `onClose`: Called on Escape (the `close` keys) while this scope is on top. The game closes it: hide or destroy the node.
- `focus`: The id of a control in this scope that takes focus each time the scope comes on top. The ring shows if it showed before. Without it, focus from another scope is cleared.

### UiCtx

```ts
interface UiCtx {
    readonly resources: Resources;
}
```

What `game` or `ctx` the kit's functions take: anything with the game's `resources`.

### UiKeys

```ts
interface UiKeys {
    readonly tab?: readonly InputBinding[];
    readonly next?: readonly InputBinding[];
    readonly previous?: readonly InputBinding[];
    readonly activate?: readonly InputBinding[];
    readonly close?: readonly InputBinding[];
}
```

The keys the kit reads, as `KeyboardEvent.code` values. An empty list turns a key off.

Members:

- `tab`: Next control; with Shift the previous one. Leaves the canvas past either end. Default `["Tab"]`.
- `next`: Next control, as `arrows` says. Default `["ArrowDown", "ArrowRight"]`.
- `previous`: Previous control, as `arrows` says. Default `["ArrowUp", "ArrowLeft"]`.
- `activate`: Activates the focused control. Default `["Enter", "NumpadEnter", "Space"]`. Left to the game while nothing is focused.
- `close`: Calls the top modal scope's `onClose`. Default `["Escape"]`. Left to the game while no scope is open.

### UiOptions

```ts
interface UiOptions {
    readonly pixi?: Pixi2DPlugin;
    readonly root?: Container;
    readonly keys?: UiKeys;
    readonly arrows?: "wrap" | "linear" | "clear";
    readonly tapFocus?: "focus" | "clear";
    readonly blurFocus?: "keep" | "clear";
    readonly focusRing?: FocusRingDrawer | false;
    readonly summary?: string | ((ctx: SystemCtx) => string | null | undefined);
    readonly hint?: string;
    readonly actions?: readonly ActionType[];
    readonly onAction?: (ctx: SystemCtx, action: ActionType) => boolean | void;
}
```

What the `ui()` plugin takes: `pixi` (the `pixi2d()` plugin) in a game, or `root` in a test game, then keys, arrows and focus behaviour.

Members:

- `pixi`: The `pixi2d()` plugin, listed before `ui` in `plugins`. Controls live under its `root` and `backdrop`.
- `root`: Instead of `pixi`: the container controls live under, whose local units are the logical units `ctx.input.pointer` reports. For a test game, which has no renderer.
- `arrows`: How the `next` and `previous` keys move focus. `"wrap"` (the default): round from the last control to the first, only while a control has focus or a modal scope is open. `"linear"`: stop at the first and last control, and from no focus go to the first (`next`) or last (`previous`); the keys are the kit's whenever a control is live. `"clear"`: as `"linear"`, but past the first or last control focus goes to none, staying on the canvas, so the next key starts again from no focus.
- `tapFocus`: What a pointer press does to focus. `"focus"` (the default): a press on a control focuses it with no ring, and a press elsewhere keeps focus. `"clear"`: every press clears focus, so Enter after a tap is the game's again.
- `blurFocus`: What the canvas losing keyboard focus does to focus. `"keep"` (the default): focus stays and the ring is hidden, so returning to the canvas resumes on the same control. `"clear"`: focus is cleared in every frame that starts with the canvas blurred, so it starts again from none.
- `focusRing`: Replaces the default ring, or `false` for none.
- `summary`: The canvas's `aria-label` while no modal scope is open. A function is called each frame and may return nothing to leave the canvas's own label. Without it the canvas keeps its own.
- `hint`: The canvas's `aria-description` while controls exist and none has focus.
- `actions`: The game's own actions, read in the kit's ordered pass: each press goes to `onAction` in the order it was typed among the kit's keys and pointer presses, so a key that opens a sheet and an Escape after it in the same frame act in that order. Needs `onAction`.
- `onAction`: Called inside `fenrir.ui.preUpdate` for each press of one of `actions` that the kit did not act on itself (a key the kit uses acts first, under its own rules, and a pointer press on a control is the kit's even when `passThrough` leaves it unconsumed). The kit reads the display tree again after it returns, so controls and scopes drawn here are live for the next key. Return `true` to consume the press: later systems do not see it.

## Added to core types when imported

Importing `fenrir-ts/ui` adds these members to core types for the whole program.

### AssetKinds

```ts

}
```

### AssetStoreConfig

```ts

    texture2DLoaders?: {
        [name: string]: PixiTextureLoaderConfig;
    };
}
```

```ts

    loadTexture2D(key: AssetKey, url: string): Promise<void>;
    getTexture2D(key: AssetKey): Promise<PixiTexture>;

}
```

### AssetStore

```ts

    loadTexture2D(key: AssetKey, url: string): Promise<void>;
    requestTexture2D(key: AssetKey, url: string): Texture2DHandle;
```

- `requestTexture2D`: Reuses an active or ready request for the same key and URL. Request again to retry a failure.

<!-- skills/fenrir/api/audio.md -->

# `fenrir-ts/audio` API reference

Generated from the TSDoc in the source by `scripts/api-reference.mjs`. Do not edit: run `pnpm api:reference`.

Sounds, buses, the unlock policy, the `audio` asset kind and the Web Audio and test backends.

Peer packages: none. Import from `fenrir-ts/audio` only, never from `dist/` or a source path.

## Contents

- Functions: [`audio`](#audio), [`defineSound`](#definesound), [`playSound`](#playsound), [`stopSound`](#stopsound), [`testAudio`](#testaudio), [`unlockAudio`](#unlockaudio), [`webAudio`](#webaudio)
- Constants: [`AudioState`](#audiostate), [`AudioUnlocked`](#audiounlocked)
- Types: [`AudioBackend`](#audiobackend), [`AudioBus`](#audiobus), [`AudioClip`](#audioclip), [`AudioCtx`](#audioctx), [`AudioOptions`](#audiooptions), [`AudioVoice`](#audiovoice), [`NoParams`](#noparams), [`PlayedSound`](#playedsound), [`PlayOptions`](#playoptions), [`SoundOptions`](#soundoptions), [`SoundType`](#soundtype), [`Synth`](#synth), [`TestAudio`](#testaudio), [`TestAudioOptions`](#testaudiooptions), [`VoiceRequest`](#voicerequest)
- [Added to core types when imported](#added-to-core-types-when-imported)

## Functions

### audio

```ts
function audio(options?: AudioOptions): Plugin;
```

Plays sounds: `playSound`, `stopSound` and `unlockAudio` need it. It adds the `AudioState`
resource, the loader for `audio` assets (so a manifest preloads samples with progress), and
two systems: `fenrir.audio.init`, which starts output at once where autoplay is allowed or
after a previous run unlocked it, and suspends output while the page is hidden, and
`fenrir.audio.postUpdate`, which applies volume and mute changes each frame.

Output starts inside the first user gesture on the canvas (through `input.onGesture`), with no
game code. When a run stops, every sound stops and output is suspended; the next run resumes it
without a new gesture.

```ts
const game = await createGame({ canvas, plugins: [audio(), pixi2d()] });
const test = await createTestGame({ seed: 1, plugins: [audio({ backend: testAudio() })] });
```

### defineSound

```ts
function defineSound<P extends object = NoParams>(name: string, options: SoundOptions<P>): SoundType<P>;
```

Defines a sound: a sample (an `audio` asset of a manifest, by name) or a synthesized sound,
with its bus, volume, looping and how many may sound at once. Plain data, declared once at
module level; play it from systems with `playSound`. The name is namespaced: `myGame.tap`.

```ts
const Tap = defineSound("myGame.tap", { sample: "tap", volume: 0.8 });
const Theme = defineSound("myGame.theme", { sample: "theme", bus: "music", loop: true });
const Blip = defineSound("myGame.blip", { synth: blip, limit: 2 });
// A synth with parameters gets all of them here; a play passes only the ones that differ.
const Tone = defineSound("myGame.tone", { synth: tone, params: { hz: 440, length: 0.1 } });
```

### playSound

```ts
function playSound<P extends object>(ctx: AudioCtx, sound: SoundType<P>, options?: PlayOptions<P>): boolean;
```

Plays `sound` now. Returns whether it is playing, or, for a looping sound, playing or queued.

Until a user gesture has started output (and while the page is hidden), a one-shot is dropped,
not queued: a tap sound played seconds late reads as a bug. A looping sound (music, ambience)
is queued instead and starts when output runs. A looping sound plays once at a time, so playing
it again while it plays or waits does nothing. A one-shot over its sound's `limit` stops that
sound's oldest instance. A sample that is not loaded yet is dropped and logged once.

`params` reach a synth sound's synth, laid over the sound's own `params`. A queued loop keeps
the parameters it was played with.

Throws for an unknown bus, a volume or rate that is not a finite number (above 0 for rate), or
`params` given for a sample sound.

```ts
playSound(ctx, Tap, { volume: 0.5, rate: ctx.random.next() * 0.2 + 0.9 });
playSound(ctx, Tone, { params: { hz: 440 * 2 ** (combo / 12) } }); // length stays 0.1
```

### stopSound

```ts
function stopSound<P extends object>(ctx: AudioCtx, sound: SoundType<P>, options?: {
    fade?: number;
}): void;
```

Stops every instance of `sound`, fading out over `fade` seconds (default 0, at once), and
removes it from the queue. It counts as stopped at once, so playing it again starts afresh
while the old instance fades.

### testAudio

```ts
function testAudio(options?: TestAudioOptions): TestAudio;
```

A backend for tests: no Web Audio, nothing is heard. Output is locked until a gesture
(`game.input.pointerDown`, `pointerUp` or `press` in a test game) unless `autoplay` is set, and
starts synchronously. Decoding returns a clip with `duration: 1`.

```ts
const sounds = testAudio();
const game = await createTestGame({ seed: 1, plugins: [audio({ backend: sounds })] });
await game.start();
game.input.pointerDown(10, 10); // the first gesture unlocks output
game.step();
expect(sounds.played.map((p) => p.sound)).toEqual(["myGame.tap"]);
```

### unlockAudio

```ts
function unlockAudio(ctx: AudioCtx): void;
```

Starts output from inside a user gesture the engine does not see, such as a click on an HTML
button over the canvas. The engine already does this for every gesture on the canvas, so most
games never call it. Does nothing while no run is going, or once output runs.

### webAudio

```ts
function webAudio(): AudioBackend;
```

The default audio backend: one `AudioContext`, a gain node per bus into a master gain node.
The context is created inside the first `start()`, which the engine calls inside a user
gesture, so no browser warns that it was not allowed to start. Samples decoded before then
decode on an `OfflineAudioContext`.

## Constants

### AudioState

```ts
interface AudioState {
    status: "locked" | "running" | "suspended" | "unavailable";
    muted: boolean;
    volume: number;
    buses: Record<string, AudioBus>;
    playing: Record<string, number>;
    queued: string[];
    dropped: number;
}
const AudioState: ResourceType<AudioState>;
```

The game's audio, as plain data: the value of the `AudioState` resource, which `inspect(game)`
shows. The game edits `muted`, `volume` and `buses`; they apply by the end of the frame, and to
every sound that plays. The engine writes the rest.

Members:

- `status`: `locked`: no user gesture has started output yet. `running`: sounds play. `suspended`: the page is hidden, or the game stopped, after output had started. `unavailable`: the backend cannot play.
- `muted`: Silences everything. Not saved by the engine: store it with `fenrir-ts` storage if the game keeps it.
- `volume`: Master volume, 0 to 1.
- `buses`: Each bus's volume and mute, by name.
- `playing`: Instances sounding now, by sound name. A sound that is not playing is absent.
- `queued`: Looping sounds asked for while output was not running, which start when it runs.
- `dropped`: One-shots dropped because output was not running or their sample was not loaded.

### AudioUnlocked

```ts
const AudioUnlocked: EventType<Record<string, never>>;
```

Sent once per game, when output first runs: after the first user gesture, or at startup where autoplay is allowed.

## Types

### AudioBackend

```ts
interface AudioBackend {
    readonly name: string;
    canAutoplay(): boolean;
    start(): boolean | Promise<boolean>;
    suspend(): void;
    setVolume(bus: string | null, volume: number): void;
    play(request: VoiceRequest): AudioVoice;
    decode(data: ArrayBuffer): Promise<AudioClip>;
}
```

Where sounds go: `webAudio()` by default, `testAudio()` in tests, or a host app's own output.
The engine decides what plays and when; a backend only does it.

Members:

- `canAutoplay`: Whether output may start without a user gesture. Asked when each run starts.
- `start`: Starts or resumes output. Called inside a user gesture, so it must ask the platform for output synchronously, and again when the page shows. Returns, or resolves to, whether output runs. Throws if the platform has no audio at all.
- `suspend`: Pauses output, keeping each voice where it is: the page was hidden or the game stopped.
- `setVolume`: Sets the volume of `bus`, or the master volume when `bus` is null. Called before `start` too.
- `play`: Starts a voice. Called only while output runs.
- `decode`: Decodes a fetched audio file, for the `audio` asset loader.

### AudioBus

```ts
interface AudioBus {
    volume: number;
    muted: boolean;
}
```

One bus in `AudioState`.

### AudioClip

```ts
interface AudioClip {
    readonly duration: number;
}
```

A decoded sample: an `AudioBuffer` from the Web Audio backend.

Members:

- `duration`: Seconds.

### AudioCtx

```ts
type AudioCtx = {
    readonly resources: Resources;
};
```

What the audio functions need: a `SystemCtx`, or the `Game` or `TestGame` itself.

### AudioOptions

```ts
interface AudioOptions {
    buses?: readonly string[];
    backend?: AudioBackend;
}
```

What the `audio()` plugin takes: bus names and the backend (`webAudio()` by default, `testAudio()` in tests).

Members:

- `buses`: Bus names. Defaults to `["sfx", "music"]`.
- `backend`: Defaults to `webAudio()`. Pass `testAudio()` in tests.

### AudioVoice

```ts
interface AudioVoice {
    stop(fade: number): void;
    onended: (() => void) | null;
}
```

A sound the backend is playing.

Members:

- `stop`: Fades out over `fade` seconds, then stops. 0 stops at once.
- `onended`: Set by the engine. The backend calls it once, when the voice has ended or been stopped.

### NoParams

```ts
type NoParams = Record<never, never>;
```

No per-play parameters: the default for a `Synth`, and what a sample sound has.

### PlayedSound

```ts
interface PlayedSound {
    sound: string;
    bus: string;
    volume: number;
    rate: number;
    loop: boolean;
    synth: boolean;
    params: Record<string, unknown>;
    ended: boolean;
    fade: number | null;
}
```

One voice the test backend was asked to play, in order.

Members:

- `volume`: The sound's volume times the play's: bus and master volumes are in `volumes`.
- `synth`: True for a synthesized sound. Its synth is not run: there is no context.
- `params`: The synth's parameters for this play: the sound's `params` with the play's laid over them. `{}` for a sample.
- `ended`: True once it ended on its own (`finish`) or was stopped.
- `fade`: The fade it was stopped with, or null while it plays or when it ended on its own.

### PlayOptions

```ts
interface PlayOptions<P extends object = NoParams> {
    volume?: number;
    rate?: number;
    params?: NoParams extends P ? never : Partial<NoInfer<P>>;
}
```

One play's options.

Members:

- `volume`: Multiplies the sound's volume. Defaults to 1.
- `rate`: Playback rate: 2 is an octave up and twice as fast. Defaults to 1.
- `params`: This play's parameters for a synth sound, laid over the sound's `params`: pass only the fields that differ. Typed from the sound's synth. A sample sound, or a synth without parameters, takes none.

### SoundOptions

```ts
type SoundOptions<P extends object = NoParams> = (SoundBase & {
    sample: string;
    synth?: never;
    params?: never;
}) | (SoundBase & {
    synth: Synth<P>;
    sample?: never;
} & ParamsOption<P>);
```

What `defineSound` takes: a `sample` (an `audio` asset name) or a `synth`, plus bus, volume, loop and voice limit.

### SoundType

```ts
interface SoundType<P extends object = NoParams> {
    readonly name: string;
    readonly sample: string | null;
    readonly synth: Synth<P> | null;
    readonly params: Readonly<P>;
    readonly bus: string;
    readonly volume: number;
    readonly loop: boolean;
    readonly limit: number;
}
```

A sound, made by `defineSound`. Plain data apart from `synth`. `P` is its synth's parameters,
which `playSound` takes as `params`; a sample sound, or a synth without parameters, has `NoParams`.

Members:

- `name`: Namespaced, such as `myGame.tap`. Counts in `AudioState.playing` are by this name.
- `sample`: The audio asset it plays, by its name in a manifest, or null for a synthesized sound.
- `params`: The synth's parameters for a play that passes none: `params` from `defineSound`, frozen. `{}` for a sample.
- `volume`: 0 to 1 and above, multiplied by each play's volume.
- `loop`: Repeats until stopped. A looping sound plays once at a time: playing it again while it plays does nothing.
- `limit`: Instances that may sound at once. Playing one more stops the oldest.

### Synth

```ts
type Synth<P extends object = NoParams> = (audio: AudioContext, output: AudioNode, play: {
    readonly rate: number;
    readonly params: Readonly<P>;
}) => AudioScheduledSourceNode;
```

Builds a synthesized sound on the context: creates its nodes, connects the last to `output`,
starts them and returns the source that ends last, so the engine knows when the sound ended and
can stop it. `rate` is the play's rate, 1 by default; scale frequencies by it if it matters.

`params` are the play's parameters, typed by `P`: the sound's `params` from `defineSound`, with
the fields `playSound` passed laid over them. So one sound plays in several variants (a pitch
per combo step, a timbre per pickup) instead of one sound per variant.

```ts
const blip: Synth = (audio, output, { rate }) => {
  const osc = audio.createOscillator();
  osc.frequency.value = 880 * rate;
  osc.connect(output);
  osc.start();
  osc.stop(audio.currentTime + 0.08);
  return osc;
};
const tone: Synth<{ hz: number; length: number }> = (audio, output, { params }) => {
  const osc = audio.createOscillator();
  osc.frequency.value = params.hz;
  osc.connect(output);
  osc.start();
  osc.stop(audio.currentTime + params.length);
  return osc;
};
```

### TestAudio

```ts
interface TestAudio extends AudioBackend {
    readonly played: PlayedSound[];
    readonly volumes: Record<string, number>;
    readonly running: boolean;
    finish(sound?: string): void;
}
```

An audio backend with no Web Audio, for `createTestGame`. Records what plays.

Members:

- `played`: Every voice played, oldest first.
- `volumes`: The volumes the engine set: `master`, then each bus by name. Muted is 0.
- `running`: Whether output runs: started and not suspended.
- `finish`: Ends playing voices as if their samples finished: all of them, or those of `sound`.

### TestAudioOptions

```ts
interface TestAudioOptions {
    autoplay?: boolean;
    unavailable?: boolean;
}
```

What `testAudio()` takes: whether it can autoplay, or is unavailable.

Members:

- `autoplay`: Output may start without a gesture, as where autoplay is allowed. Defaults to false: locked until a gesture.
- `unavailable`: The platform has no audio: `start` throws, and the engine reports `unavailable`. Defaults to false.

### VoiceRequest

```ts
interface VoiceRequest {
    readonly sound: string;
    readonly bus: string;
    readonly clip: AudioClip | null;
    readonly synth: Synth<object> | null;
    readonly params?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
    readonly volume: number;
    readonly rate: number;
    readonly loop: boolean;
}
```

What the backend is asked to play.

Members:

- `clip`: The decoded sample, for a sample sound.
- `params`: The synth's parameters for this play: the sound's `params` with the play's laid over them. The engine always sets it (`{}` for a sample); optional so requests built by hand still type-check.
- `volume`: The sound's volume times the play's.

## Added to core types when imported

Importing `fenrir-ts/audio` adds these members to core types for the whole program.

### AssetKinds

```ts
interface AssetKinds {
    audio: AudioClip;
}
```

- `audio`: A decoded sample, loaded by the `audio()` plugin's loader. Declared in a manifest as `{ kind: "audio", src }`.
